meaning: The full 32-entry hardware palette PROM (82s123.7f). Each byte is a resistor-DAC-encoded RGB colour (MAME pacman_palette PALETTE_INIT: 3-3-2 weighted resistors, `-BBGGGRRR`); byte 0 is the black entry (all bits low). This claim pins the raw ROM bytes; the RGB decode is a later task's job.

Colour-lookup PROM (82s126.4a) 4-byte run at set index 0 — each byte is a 4-bit index into PALETTE-ALL, one per pixel colour-code within a colour set (MAME pacman_palette colourtable build). All-zero here (background/black across all four codes); which tile/sprite colour-select maps to set 0 is a later task's decode.
Colour-lookup PROM (82s126.4a) 4-byte run at set index 1 — a candidate maze/dot colour set (non-zero entries 15,11,1). Pins the raw bytes; which glyph uses this set is a later task's decode.
Colour-lookup PROM (82s126.4a) 4-byte run at set index 16 — a candidate sprite (ghost/Pac-Man) colour set (entries 14,0,11). Pins the raw bytes; which sprite uses this set is a later task's decode.
Tile ROM (pacman.5e) 16-byte run at tile index 16 (0x10) — a candidate dot (pellet) glyph anchor for the maze-tile decode. Pins the raw ROM bytes; the wall/dot tile-index map is a later task's job.

Tile ROM (pacman.5e) 16-byte run at tile index 20 (0x14) — a candidate energizer (power pellet) glyph anchor, a filled circular pattern larger than TILE-DOT. Pins the raw ROM bytes; the tile-index map is a later task's job.

Tile ROM (pacman.5e) 16-byte run at tile index 64 (0x40) — a candidate maze wall/corner glyph anchor (all-zero, likely a blank/edge piece). Pins the raw ROM bytes; wall-orientation semantics are a later task's decode.

Tile ROM (pacman.5e) 16-byte run at tile index 68 (0x44) — a candidate maze wall/corner glyph anchor with a diagonal-line bit pattern. Pins the raw ROM bytes; wall-orientation semantics are a later task's decode.
